workstream: D — external-baseline qualification and adapter readiness
purpose: Records, for each external method, which COMPOSE Claim-4 sub-capability it is a valid comparator for, what matched budget means for it, and where the comparison stops being fair. Every capability cell carries a primary source or is marked UNVERIFIED. This registry contains no results and authorises no run.

evidence_standard.rule: A capability cell asserting YES, NO or PARTIAL must cite a primary source: the paper with a section, or the official repository with a file or symbol. UNVERIFIED is a legitimate value and must record what was searched.
evidence_standard.not_admissible: Secondary sources as sole evidence; a capability the official code could be modified to support; plausible inference from method family.
evidence_standard.openreview_gap: OpenReview forums for MARS (kHSu4ebxFXY), DDSBM (tQyh0gnfqW), HN-GFN (uoG1fLIK2s) and PMO (yCZRdI0Y7G) are behind a bot challenge and returned HTTP 403. No reviewer discussion was read for any method. Venues were confirmed from proceedings pages and paper footers instead.

compose_subcapabilities.C4a_static_optimization: source-conditioned static property optimization under a matched oracle budget; a competitive result is wanted, not a novelty claim
compose_subcapabilities.C4b_exact_target: exact-target recovery from a source under a finite edit budget; DONE, SEALED AND CLOSED (greedy 26/65, verified remaining-budget rollout 40/65, learned top-1 + verification 40/65 at ~35% of continuation evaluations)
compose_subcapabilities.C4c_retargeting: same-prefix dynamic retargeting: the goal changes mid-trajectory and the process continues from the realized molecule under a finite remaining budget, with the reference process frozen; IN FLIGHT
compose_subcapabilities.C4d_pathwise: pathwise constraints: a labeled motif preserved at every committed intermediate state, on a support that includes deletions and topology changes; PLANNED

frozen_process_claim: R_theta is not retrained between C4a, C4b, C4c and C4d. A baseline that reaches C4c or C4d only by retraining per objective does not refute that claim; a baseline that reaches them without retraining does. That is why objective_specific_retraining is a required column and why the escalation list below matters more than any table of results.

compose_claim_scoping.headline: 'Future-aware control helps' is NOT a universal COMPOSE claim. It is ESTABLISHED on hard exact-target recovery and MEASURED ABSENT on an easy target-free property goal. Every fairness contract below is written against that scoping, and a comparison that ignores it will be read as testing a claim COMPOSE does not make.

where_it_is_established.task: C4b exact-target recovery from a source under a finite edit budget, sealed panel, 65 endpoint-clean pairs
where_it_is_established.result: greedy 26/65 (40%) vs verified remaining-budget rollout 40/65 (62%); paired difference +21.5 pp [12.3, 33.5], rescuing 35.9% [21.2, 52.8] of greedy's 39 failures. Learned top-1 prioritisation matches the recovery count at ~35% of the continuation evaluations.

where_it_is_measured_absent.task: target-free bounded developability goal (cLogP box + QED floor) after a same-prefix goal switch, 3+3 horizon
where_it_is_measured_absent.result: greedy 28/30 vs verified 28/30, binary headroom 0. Continuous utility favours verified (mean +0.0361, higher on 23/30, lower on 0) but the DIRECTION is guaranteed by the policy-improvement theorem and only the magnitude is admissible: +3.2% of typical post-switch movement, never enough to flip a success. Gate CLOSED; subclaim B dropped for this goal under the pre-committed anti-tuning rule.
where_it_is_measured_absent.artifact: diagnostics/retarget_calibration_result_3plus3_fixed.json, cohort e402e318; design and gate in docs/RETARGETING_SAME_PREFIX_DESIGN.md
where_it_is_measured_absent.corroborating: The earlier C0 planning-signal probe on DRD2 was also negative: 8/14 sacrificial actions won against a null of 0.5, mean fresh regret -0.021 (diagnostics/editing_v2_experiment_c0_planning_signal_preregistered.json).

consequences_for_every_comparison_in_thi: C4a static optimization on easy target-free property goals -- which is what PMO's DRD2/GSK3b/JNK3 tasks and the developability box are -- is a COMPETITIVENESS SANITY CHECK, not a claim-bearing test. A baseline winning there refutes nothing about future-aware control, because COMPOSE does not claim future-aware control helps there. A COMPOSE win there supports 'the substrate plus ordinary control is competitive', which is a weaker and different sentence.

The regime where a baseline would actually have to beat COMPOSE is hard, bounded-feasibility, finite-remaining-budget search where myopic control provably fails -- i.e. C4b. On that regime none of the six methods is even applicable: GraphXForm cannot delete an atom, MARS has no remaining-budget concept, GraphGA does not preserve the source, REINVENT and HN-GFN have no intermediate molecular states, and DDSBM has no oracle in the loop. That is a scope fact and must be reported as N/A, not as a COMPOSE win.

C4c retargeting is therefore about INTERVENTION RESPONSIVENESS and PREFIX REUSE, not about post-switch planning quality. The comparison against REINVENT staged learning and MARS-restart is on post-switch oracle cost and whether a restart was required -- exactly what docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md Experiment 6 already says: 'A strong result is not merely a higher endpoint score. It is comparable or better final quality with substantially lower post-switch oracle cost and no restart.'

Do not choose a comparison task because it makes greedy fail. The anti-tuning rule in docs/RETARGETING_SAME_PREFIX_DESIGN.md is binding on this lane too: the goal is fixed once, and a goal on which future-aware control shows no advantage is reported, not replaced.
compose_claim_scoping.what_this_does_not_weaken: The frozen-process property is untouched by this scoping. One R_theta serves C4a, C4b, C4c and C4d with no retraining between them, and that is the claim the escalation list tests. Whether the controller on top of it is future-aware or myopic on a given goal is a separate, per-goal question that has now been answered in both directions.

methods.native_task: Annealed MCMC sampling from a fixed unnormalized multi-objective target pi(x) = sum_k s_k(x) over molecules, with an adaptive fragment-edit proposal trained online during the run. Paper section 3.1: 'given K properties of interest, the desired molecular distribution can be formulated as a combination of all objectives'. Each Markov-chain state is a complete molecule.

source_conditioning.evidence: main.py: `if config['mols_init']: mols = load_mols(...); mols = random.choices(mols, k=config['num_mols'])`. A one-line SMILES file therefore replicates one exact molecule into every chain. Sampler.sample(run_dir, mols_init) also accepts a per-chain list directly. Default with no flag is ethane 'CC' for every chain (paper section 4.1: 'The sampling paths are all starting with an identical molecule "C-C"').
source_conditioning.note: Works with stock code but is undocumented and untested by the authors; the README ships no init file and describes no such usage.

objective_specific_retraining.evidence: There is no pretraining stage at all. The proposal is trained online during the run on edits that improved the score — paper section 3.2 'we propose to train the model on-the-fly during the sampling process in an adaptive manner'; sampler.py computes `indices = [i for i in range(len(old_mols)) if new_scores[i] > old_scores[i]]` and takes at most 25 gradient steps per MCMC step. Every run starts from a randomly initialised editor (main.py, inside the per-run loop).
objective_specific_retraining.note: No offline retraining is needed for a new objective, but the online adaptation cost is paid inside every run and is funded by oracle calls.

intermediate_states_exposed.evidence: Every chain state is a complete valid molecule: proposals are checked by common/chem.py::check_validity (Chem.SanitizeMol) and an invalid proposal leaves the chain on its current molecule (proposal.py sets new_mols[i] = mols[i]). Adds are capped at 40 atoms; deletes are rejected if the skeleton would have no bonds.
intermediate_states_exposed.note: The states exist but MARS keeps no trajectory record; the accepted-state sequence must be logged by an adapter.

pathwise_constraints_native.evidence: Exhaustive grep of the official repository for mask|constrain|scaffold|substruct|motif|frozen|freeze|protect|MolFromSmarts returns only training-loss masks in proposal/models/editor_basic.py (mask_del, mask_add, mask_arm), which select which nodes and edges contribute to the cross-entropy. No GetSubstructMatch, no SMARTS, no atom freezing. break_bond (common/chem.py) may delete any single-bond-attached fragment, including a motif we wanted preserved.
pathwise_constraints_native.note: Enforcing a motif would mean modifying Proposal.propose. That is our work, not a native capability, and would be a reported deviation. See near_misses: MARS AFFORDS pathwise enforcement because all its states are molecules, which is a weaker and different statement.

dynamic_goal_switching_native.evidence: Objectives are parsed once (main.py: config['objectives'] = config['objectives'].split(',')), consumed at Estimator and Sampler construction (estimator.py: self.objectives = config['objectives']; sampler.py builds score_wght/score_succ/score_clip), and the sampling loop contains no hook to swap the estimator, the weights or the clips. A full-text search of the paper for switch|warm-start|resume|restart|retrain|transfer|mid-run|new objective returns only an unrelated citation title. There is also no resume or checkpoint machinery.
dynamic_goal_switching_native.note: Zero support in both paper and code. This is a hard NO and it directly answers the lead's question.

restart_at_supplied_state_under_new_obje.evidence: Achievable with stock code: construct a new Estimator with the new objectives and call Sampler.sample(run_dir, mols_init=[switch_molecule] * num_mols). Both entry points exist (main.py, sampler.py) and no patch is required. But it is a RESTART, not a continuation: the editor is randomly re-initialised because no checkpoint path exists, the imitation dataset D starts empty, and the temperature counter resets.
restart_at_supplied_state_under_new_obje.note: This is the arm EXPERIMENT_PLAN Experiment 6 already names as 'MARS restarted at the switch state where technically possible'. It is technically possible.

oracle_accounting.definition: One molecule scoring per chain per step, expanding to K property evaluations (estimator.py loops over self.objectives).
oracle_accounting.counts_rejected_proposals: YES — all candidates are scored at sampler.py before the accept/reject loop and rejected scores are discarded. When a proposal is invalid the current molecule is substituted and redundantly re-scored.
oracle_accounting.training_phase_oracle_calls: Not separable. The online proposal training is driven by the same score comparisons, so every training signal is already inside the per-step scoring count. There is no separate training phase.
oracle_accounting.default_total_budget: Code defaults: 1000 chains x (1 + 1000 steps) = 1,001,000 molecule scorings per run = 4,004,000 property evaluations at 4 objectives, x10 runs. Paper settings N=5000 chains and ~550 steps = 2,755,000 molecule scorings per run. There is no cache anywhere (grep for cache|memo|lru_cache|seen returns only torch.cuda.empty_cache).
oracle_accounting.caching_note: MARS re-evaluates revisited molecules. An adapter must add the shared-semantics cache the fairness contract requires, and must report cache hits separately so the comparison is not silently changed.

methods.edit_budget: One edit attempt per chain per step. Code defaults give ~10^6 attempted edits per run; paper settings ~2.75x10^6. Early stopping via PATIENCE=100 when neither the PM product nor the average score improves by 0.01.

fairness_contract.matched_quantity: Property-oracle calls, counting every scored candidate including rejected proposals and including the redundant re-scoring MARS performs on invalid proposals. Edits are the secondary matched quantity: one attempted edit per chain per step against one committed COMPOSE edit. Wall time reported, never matched.
fairness_contract.not_fair_because: MARS's designed regime is ~10^6 molecule scorings per run. A COMPOSE-matched budget of hundreds to thousands puts it three orders of magnitude below the setting its adaptive proposal was built to exploit, because that proposal only becomes useful after online training on many accepted edits. Reporting only the matched-budget number would misrepresent the method, so BOTH a matched-budget row AND MARS's native-regime row are required, with the gap stated. Support also differs: MARS edits at fragment granularity from a ChEMBL-derived 1000-fragment vocabulary, COMPOSE at canonical-successor granularity of the frozen rewrite kernel. Equal support must never be claimed.
fairness_contract.n_a_metrics: All pathwise metrics are N/A: MARS has no constraint mechanism, and a motif-preserving filter added by us would be a deviation, not the method.

methods.native_task: Single-objective de-novo molecular graph design by a pretrained graph transformer that iteratively adds atoms and bonds, fine-tuned per objective by self-improvement. Abstract: 'Our approach iteratively modifies a molecular graph by adding atoms and bonds, which ensures chemical validity and facilitates the incorporation of structural constraints.' Demonstrated on 20 GuacaMol goal-directed tasks and two liquid-liquid-extraction solvent-design tasks.

MoleculeDesign.from_smiles(..., do_finish=False) replays the molecule as an action prefix without issuing the terminate action, so the design arrives at action level 0 un-terminated and the model continues modifying it. Paper section 3.3.3 seeds design from 'the best molecule from COSMObase 2020'.

objective_specific_retraining.evidence: Required for the paper's reported results. Section 2.2: 'In each epoch, the current policy is used to generate a set of action sequences, from which the best sequences are selected as pseudo-labels to serve as the dataset for supervised training'; 'we sample batches of intermediate molecules and train the network with a cross-entropy loss to predict the next action'. main.py freezes all parameters, unfreezes only virtual_atom_linear and bond_atom_linear, and runs loss.backward(); optimizer.step(). objective_type is a single global config field consumed by the evaluator, so it is one fine-tuning run per objective.
objective_specific_retraining.note: Head-only fine-tuning, but it IS a gradient update per objective. A pure-search path exists (num_epochs = 0) and is not what the paper reports; main.py warns if no checkpoint is supplied on that path.

intermediate_states_exposed.evidence: Full action history is retained (self.history in molecule_design.py) and persisted per molecule as action_seq alongside SMILES and objective (core/gumbeldore_dataset.py); keep_intermediate_trajectories defaults True so intermediate terminable nodes enter the candidate set. BUT a complete terminable molecule exists only at action level 0 — is_terminable() returns `self.current_action_level == 0 and not self.synthesis_done`, and assert_feasible enforces full connectivity only at level 0. Between levels 0->1->2 the graph carries a dangling unbonded atom.
intermediate_states_exposed.note: Valid molecule at every atom/bond-completion boundary, not at every raw action index. Usable for pathwise metrics only if scored at level-0 boundaries.

pathwise_constraints_native.evidence: Genuine per-step masking exists: update_action_mask() is recomputed after every action (take_action ends with it) and masked_log_probs_for_current_action_level sets logits[mask] = -inf before softmax. Section 2.1: 'we mask any action in the policy that would lead to a violation of valence constraints ... we set the corresponding probability to zero in the distribution predicted by the policy (before re-normalizing the distribution).' BUT the exhaustive maskable set in the released code is: atom type allowed/disallowed, max_num_atoms, remaining valence per atom, no self-bonding, no re-bonding an already-bonded pair, bond order at most the minimum free valence. The paper's ring-size and disallowed-bonding-pattern constraints are implemented instead as a TERMINAL filter in molecule_evaluator.py::infeasible_by_special_constraints, asserted on mol.synthesis_done and returning -inf. There is no SMARTS or substructure matching anywhere in the repository.
pathwise_constraints_native.note: The mechanism is pathwise; the expressible constraint class does not include labeled subgraphs. This is the single most important correction to the Workstream C assumption that GraphXForm is already a native pathwise-constraint baseline.

dynamic_goal_switching_native.evidence: objective_type is a single immutable config string (config.py) read once when MoleculeObjectiveEvaluator is constructed (main.py, and per worker in core/gumbeldore_dataset.py). No code path re-targets the objective mid-trajectory; a repo-wide search returns only the config comment. No discussion of mid-trajectory objective change appears in any retrieved section of the paper.
dynamic_goal_switching_native.note: The code absence is verified; the paper silence is an absence of evidence, recorded as such.

oracle_accounting.definition: Every leaf of every TASAR beam round is scored: core/incremental_sbs.py calls batch_leaf_evaluation_fn on all beam leaves, wired to objective_evaluator.predict_objective. With keep_intermediate_trajectories True, intermediate terminable nodes also enter the leaf set and are scored.

oracle_accounting.training_phase_oracle_calls: YES, and they dominate. Dataset generation IS the search and runs once per epoch inside train_for_one_epoch before every gradient step. Order of magnitude: beam_width x TASAR rounds x epochs.
oracle_accounting.default_total_budget: None numeric. The paper explicitly rejects an oracle-call budget (section 3.1: 'to provide a practical comparison between our method and competing approaches, each design run is executed until convergence or until a maximum wall-clock time of eight hours is reached'). Governed by wall_clock_limit (8 h in the paper, None in shipped config) and num_epochs = 1000.

fairness_contract.matched_quantity: Property-oracle calls, counting every beam leaf scored AND every call consumed by per-objective fine-tuning. TWO totals must be reported — with and without the fine-tuning phase — because the choice changes which method looks efficient and a reviewer may reasonably object to either convention. Edit budget is N/A and must be printed as N/A: GraphXForm's actions are atom and bond additions, not molecule-to-molecule edits.
fairness_contract.not_fair_because: Three asymmetries. (1) The action space is strictly constructive — no atom or bond removal exists and the paper defers removal to future work (section 3.3.3) — so on any task requiring a deletion it cannot reach the answer at all. That is a scope difference, not a quality result, and must be stated wherever it binds. (2) The paper deliberately does not operate under an oracle budget and argues its objectives are cheap; imposing one runs it outside its designed protocol. (3) Its per-objective fine-tuning has no COMPOSE counterpart because R_theta is frozen, so the comparison is between a method that pays a training cost per objective and one that does not — which is the claim under test, not a nuisance to normalise away.
fairness_contract.n_a_metrics: Edit budget N/A. Labeled-motif pathwise metrics are measurable but must be reported as the OUTCOME of an unconstrained run, never as a constrained arm, because the released code cannot mask on substructures.

methods.native_task: A discrete Schrodinger bridge between two graph DISTRIBUTIONS, solved by iterative Markovian fitting. Only the two marginals are prescribed; the coupling is what the method solves for. Section F.2.2 states the contrast explicitly: 'except for DDSBM, all of them assume that suitable molecule pairs have already been identified to be provided.' At sampling time a specific source graph is transported, but the network never sees a target — the target is baked into the weights.

But the only network inputs are {X_t, E_t, y_t, t, node_mask} and y is a zero-width tensor in every dataset file (y = torch.zeros(size=(1, 0))). Conditioning exists on the source endpoint only; the target lives in the weights.

objective_specific_retraining.evidence: The objective IS the terminal distribution. For ZINC the only encoding of the objective is the logP-2 versus logP-4 split (section 5.2), and the paper states DDSBM is 'trained solely to optimize graph transformations with minimal structural alterations, without explicit knowledge on molecular properties'. A new objective means a new terminal dataset and a full retrain: 300 epochs x 6 IMF iterations on four GPUs for ZINC (Table 4).
objective_specific_retraining.note: There is no conditioning channel to exploit for zero-shot retargeting; y is zero-width.

intermediate_states_exposed.evidence: The sampler independently resamples every node and edge category at each step (sample_discrete_features then one-hot, inside `for t_int in range(0, self.T - 1)`) with no valency check, no connectivity check, no sanitisation and no rejection anywhere in the loop. Molecules are assembled only from the final state. Even the final state is not guaranteed connected: compute_validity keeps the largest fragment. Reported DBM validity on Polymer is 43.4% (Table 2). Section E.2 admits 'occasional failures in decoding into molecules'.
intermediate_states_exposed.note: Intermediates are noisy categorical graphs, not molecules. Every pathwise metric is N/A by construction.

dynamic_goal_switching_native.evidence: Three independent grounds. (1) Formulation: the object is a fixed pair of boundary distributions with a static optimal coupling, so retargeting means changing the terminal marginal, i.e. a different optimization problem. (2) API: sample_forward_bridge_batch hard-starts at t=0 from the supplied X_0 and runs the full loop; there is no start-time parameter, no way to inject a realized intermediate state, and no way to swap the model mid-loop (number_chain_steps only controls how many frames are saved for visualisation). (3) Theory: the learned generator is time-inhomogeneous and conditioned on remaining time to tau, so splicing a differently-trained model at t=k evaluates it at a time index whose bridge geometry was fitted to a different terminal distribution.

methods.native_task: Target-free multi-objective molecular optimization with Pareto coverage. HN-GFN proper is the acquisition-function optimizer inside a multi-objective Bayesian-optimization loop, not a standalone method: 'we propose a multi-objective Bayesian optimization algorithm leveraging the hypernetwork-based GFlowNets as an acquisition function optimizer, with the purpose of sampling a diverse batch of candidate molecular graphs from an approximate Pareto front.' The standalone use in section 5.1 is explicitly labelled a synthetic scenario.

dynamic_goal_switching_native.evidence: The preference vector is sampled once per rollout and held fixed for every step: main.py samples weights = Dirichlet(...).sample_n(1) before the loop and passes the same weights to generator(...) at every t, with reward computed only at termination under those weights. methods.native_task: A graph-based genetic algorithm (GB-GA) maximizing a scalar black-box score over molecules by crossover and mutation on RDKit graphs. The paper's own task is penalized logP: 'the goal is to maximize J(m): J(m) = log P(m) - SA(m) - RingPenalty(m)'. The scoring function is an argument, so it is a generic scalar maximizer.

provenance.code_reference: master. Paper ESI cites github.com/jensengroup/GB-GA/tree/v0.0. Jensen, Chem. Sci. 10(12) 3567-3572 (2019), PMID 30996948, PMC6438151, CC BY 3.0. The benchmark-standard wrapper is main/graph_ga/ in https://github.com/wenhao-gao/mol_opt (PMO, MIT).
provenance.license: MIT ('MIT License / Copyright (c) 2018 Jensen Group'; GitHub API spdx_id MIT). PMO wrapper also MIT.
provenance.checkpoints: None — there is no trained model.

source_conditioning.evidence: The only seeding interface is a SMILES file: GB_GA.py::make_initial_population does `population.append(random.choice(mol_list))` per individual, sampling with replacement, so a one-line SMILES file yields population_size identical copies of that molecule. There is no native source-molecule concept, flag or API. PMO's variant differs: main/graph_ga/run.py uses `starting_population = self.all_smiles[:config['population_size']]`.
source_conditioning.note: Crucially the source is NOT preserved. Abstract: 'The molecules found by the GB-GA bear little resemblance to the molecules used to construct the initial mating pool'; the Results report nearest-ZINC Tanimoto of 0.27 and 0.12.

objective_specific_retraining.evidence: There is no model and no training. Paper conclusion: 'Both the GB-GA and GB-GM-MCTS codes used in this study are freely available with the open source RDKit toolkit as the only dependence.' Changing the objective means passing a different scoring_function. Verified by import audit: no torch, tensorflow or cuda imports in GB_GA.py, crossover.py, mutate.py, scoring_functions.py or GA_logP.py.
objective_specific_retraining.note: Zero warm-up oracle cost. This makes GraphGA the cleanest budget-matched comparator in the set.

intermediate_states_exposed.evidence: Every individual is a complete RDKit-sanitized molecule and invalid products are discarded rather than carried. But the structure is a branching two-parent genealogy, not a path: reproduce() returns only the child and parentage is not persisted (the debug print of parent_A/parent_B is commented out). The only logged trajectory is high_scores — one (best_score, best_smiles) tuple per generation, a best-so-far curve, not an edit path.
intermediate_states_exposed.note: Any source-to-final lineage is a DAG with two in-edges per node. Synthesising a 'trajectory' from it and scoring pathwise metrics on it is a forbidden adaptation under this protocol.

pathwise_constraints_native.evidence: No substructure or scaffold preservation mechanism exists at any level. The only per-step filters are structural sanity checks (paper: 'Molecules with macrocycles (seven atoms or more), allene centers in rings, fewer than five heavy atoms, incorrect valences as determined by RDKit, and more non-H atoms than the target size are discarded'). Crossover actively destroys invariants: 'a crossover can occur both at non-ring and ring bonds, with equal probability and the positions of the cuts are chosen randomly', and mutate.py includes delete_atom() with SMARTS such as '[*:1]~[D1]>>[*:1]'.

dynamic_goal_switching_native.evidence: GB_GA.GA(args) unpacks a single scoring_function fixed for the whole run and `for generation in range(generations)` never re-reads it. There is no stage or phase concept.

restart_at_supplied_state_under_new_obje.evidence: Restarting with a new scoring_function and the final population written out as the seed file is mechanically possible with stock entry points, but it is not a provided feature and nothing in the paper or repository describes it.
restart_at_supplied_state_under_new_obje.note: Because GraphGA carries no learned state, a restart loses nothing except the population — which makes it the cleanest 'restart at the switch state' control arm in the set.

oracle_accounting.definition: population_size x generations, plus the initial population. Paper: 'The population size is 20 and 50 generations are used (i.e. 1000 J(m) evaluations per run).' The code also scores the initial population, giving 20 x 51 = 1020; the paper rounds to 1000.
oracle_accounting.counts_rejected_proposals: YES natively — reproduce() fills new_population to exactly population_size and calculate_scores scores all of them with no dedup before scoring, so duplicates DO consume oracle calls. Invalid children do NOT: the while loop only appends non-None children, so failed crossover or mutation is retried at zero oracle cost. Survivors are never re-scored. NOTE: under the PMO wrapper this changes — see the global fairness rules.
oracle_accounting.training_phase_oracle_calls: ZERO. There is no training phase.
oracle_accounting.default_total_budget: 1020 in the paper's reference config. Under PMO the budget is 10,000 unique valid canonical SMILES with hyperparameters population_size 120, offspring_size 70, mutation_rate 0.067.
oracle_accounting.caching_note: No native cache. PMO's Oracle.score_smi provides one via mol_buffer keyed on canonical SMILES.

REINVENT 4 paper, Methods: 'Reinforcement Learning (RL) is the main molecule optimization method in REINVENT'; 'a molecule is optimized with respect to a user defined aggregation of scoring functions'. It optimizes a distribution over molecules (the agent weights), not a designated molecule.

REINVENT 2.0: Blaschke et al., JCIM 2020, DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.0c00915, repo https://github.com/MolecularAI/Reinvent (license UNVERIFIED). For Reinforcement learning (RL) a GPU is less important because most scoring components run on the CPU. Note that if no GPU is installed in your computer the code will run on the CPU automatically.' CLI flag -d/--device.

source_conditioning.evidence: REINVENT 4 has four generators. Paper Fig. 4: 'Reinvent creates new molecules de novo i.e. from scratch, Libinvent decorates a scaffold, Linkinvent identifies a linker between two fragments and Mol2Mol optimizes molecules within a user defined similarity'; 'No input SMILES are needed for Reinvent, a scaffold is needed for Libinvent, two warheads for Linkinvent and an input molecule for Mol2Mol.'
source_conditioning.note: Important scope limits. LibInvent requires a scaffold WITH EXPLICIT ATTACHMENT POINTS, not an arbitrary complete molecule. Mol2Mol accepts a complete molecule but does not preserve it: 'importantly, the scaffold can change within the limits of the given similarity'. So exact single-molecule input exists, but only LibInvent and LinkInvent preserve the supplied fragment by construction.

objective_specific_retraining.evidence: RL fine-tuning per objective is the method. Paper, Staged learning: 'Staged learning requires both a prior and an agent model. The prior is only being used as a reference ... The agent is the model that is being trained in the run.' Cost is batch_size x steps: the shipped configs/staged_learning.toml uses batch_size 64 with min_steps 25 and max_steps 100, i.e. at most 6400 scored molecules per stage. Under PMO the entire 10,000-call budget is consumed by RL fine-tuning (main/reinvent/run.py samples config['batch_size'] per step and calls self.oracle(smiles) until self.finish).
objective_specific_retraining.note: The prior itself costs zero oracle calls — it is unsupervised likelihood pretraining on ChEMBL/PubChem. There is no zero-shot mode. An exact fixed fine-tuning cost is UNVERIFIED because it is whatever budget the user allocates.

intermediate_states_exposed.evidence: Generation is autoregressive over SMILES tokens: paper, Theory: 'All REINVENT 4 models consist of sequence-based neural network models that are parameterized to capture the probability of generating tokens t in an auto-regressive manner ... SMILES strings are generated iteratively by feeding the transformer with n-1 tokens to obtain the n-th token.' Intermediate states are token prefixes and are generally not parseable molecules. The only per-run trajectory is batch-level: a CSV written per RL epoch.
intermediate_states_exposed.note: Every pathwise metric is N/A. Treating a partially decoded SMILES prefix as an intermediate molecule is a forbidden adaptation under this protocol.

pathwise_constraints_native.evidence: Two mechanisms, neither pathwise. (a) LibInvent's scaffold and LinkInvent's warheads are held fixed as the generator template, guaranteeing the fragment in the FINAL molecule; but generation is a single input-to-output step, so 'every intermediate state' has no referent, and this does not apply to the Reinvent or Mol2Mol modes. (b) The MatchingSubstructure component is a SOFT penalty, not a constraint: reinvent_plugins/components/RDKit/comp_matching_substructure.py is tagged @add_tag('__component', 'penalty') and returns 0.5 * (1.0 + match), i.e. 0.5 when the SMARTS is absent and 1.0 when present. Molecules lacking the substructure are still generated and still score nonzero. Custom alerts run the opposite direction: a SMARTS blocklist multiplying the score by 0 or 1.

dynamic_goal_switching_native.evidence: REINVENT 4 has native staged (curriculum) learning that varies the scoring function within one run. Paper, Staged learning, verbatim: 'This is basically curriculum learning (CL) which in REINVENT 4 is implemented as a multi-stage RL. The main purpose is to allow the user to optimize a prior model conditioned on a calculated target profile by varying the scoring function in stages. ... Multiple stages can be provided at once (automatic CL). After each stage a checkpoint file is written to disk which can be used for the next stage (manual CL).' configs/staged_learning.toml ships [[stage]] blocks each with its own [stage.scoring] and chkpt_file.
dynamic_goal_switching_native.note: ESCALATED. This is the closest published thing to COMPOSE's mid-run goal change and a reviewer will raise it. It is PARTIAL rather than YES because (i) switching happens at stage boundaries triggered by max_score or max_steps, not at an arbitrary chosen step, (ii) what carries across the switch is the AGENT POLICY, not a realized molecular history — there is no in-flight molecule to continue from, and (iii) the agent must re-adapt by further RL steps after the switch, which is retraining.

restart_at_supplied_state_under_new_obje.evidence: Both halves exist natively and compose. A supplied molecule enters via Mol2Mol (or a scaffold via LibInvent), and a new objective is applied by writing a new [[stage]] scoring block and resuming from the checkpoint: paper, 'When a run terminates ... a checkpoint file representing the current state of the agent will be written to disk. This checkpoint can be reused as the agent later'; configs/staged_learning.toml: 'it is also possible to continue a run from any checkpoint file that is generated during the run (manual CL).'
restart_at_supplied_state_under_new_obje.note: ESCALATED. Unlike MARS and GraphXForm, the restart is warm: the adapted policy survives the objective change.

oracle_accounting.definition: REINVENT counts STEPS, not oracle calls. Molecules scored per step equals batch_size. The scoring component is invoked only on valid, non-duplicate, non-filtered, non-cached SMILES: reinvent/scoring/scorer.py computes valid_mask = np.logical_and(invalid_mask, duplicate_mask), and compute_scores.py documents 'get the smiles that need to be scored in this call — this is all inputs except for masked smiles or those in cache'.
oracle_accounting.counts_rejected_proposals: NO natively. Paper: 'Scores for each SMILES string will be cached on a per-component basis to avoid the re-computation of scores. ... Duplicates are marked as such and handled by the caching mechanism', and 'SMILES that do not pass those filters will not be subjected to score evaluation and consequently all component scores will be zero.' Every sampled molecule occupies a batch slot and receives a score value, but the oracle is not invoked for it. Under PMO the same effective rule applies from the other side (Oracle.score_smi counts unique valid canonical SMILES).
oracle_accounting.training_phase_oracle_calls: ALL of them. There is no separate search phase: the RL fine-tuning IS the optimization, so the entire budget is training-phase.
oracle_accounting.default_total_budget: No native budget concept. Shipped example: batch_size 64, min_steps 25, max_steps 100 per stage, so at most 6400 scored molecules per stage, summed over stages. Under PMO: 10,000 unique valid canonical SMILES, hyperparameters learning_rate 0.0005, batch_size 64, sigma 500, experience_replay 24.
oracle_accounting.caching_note: REINVENT caches per scoring component by design. Its diversity filter additionally zero-scores every repeat of a canonical SMILES globally, which is a behaviour change, not just an accounting one.

methods.edit_budget: N/A. There are no molecule-to-molecule edits; a generation is a full SMILES decode. Steps and batch size are the only budget knobs.

adapter.note: Two distinct adapters are needed and must not be conflated: the PMO-wrapped 2.0-era model for oracle-efficiency parity, and REINVENT 4 for the staged-learning arm.

Adapter B (staged learning): REINVENT 4 with a two-stage staged_learning.toml, Mol2Mol or LibInvent input, and the COMPOSE objective as a custom scoring component. This is the only external arm that natively changes objective mid-run and it must be run to be honest about the C4c claim.
Declare and record the oracle convention. REINVENT's native caching means its raw call count is not comparable to MARS's without adjustment.

compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what: Changes the objective within a single run and carries the adapted agent across the change. Staged (curriculum) learning is a first-class run mode whose stated purpose is 'to allow the user to optimize a prior model conditioned on a calculated target profile by varying the scoring function in stages', with a checkpoint written after each stage and reusable as the next stage's agent. This is the strongest overlap with COMPOSE's mid-run goal-change claim in the whole registry, and the paper must not say that no existing method changes objective mid-run.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.evidence: REINVENT 4, Loeffler et al., J. Cheminform. 2024 (PMC10882833), section 'Staged learning', verbatim quoted; and https://github.com/MolecularAI/REINVENT4/blob/main/configs/staged_learning.toml, which ships two [[stage]] blocks each with its own [stage.scoring] and chkpt_file.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what_compose_still_has: REINVENT re-targets a POLICY, not a realized molecule: there is no in-flight molecular state to continue from, the switch fires at a stage boundary set by max_score or max_steps rather than at an arbitrary chosen step, and the agent must re-adapt by further RL after the switch. COMPOSE's claim is a goal change at an arbitrary step of a realized molecular history, continuing from the exact current molecule under a finite remaining budget, with the reference process frozen and only the control law recomputed.

compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what: Warm restart from a supplied molecule under a new objective. A complete molecule enters via Mol2Mol (or a scaffold via LibInvent), and the run resumes from a written checkpoint with a new scoring block, so unlike MARS and GraphXForm the adapted policy survives the objective change.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.evidence: REINVENT 4 paper Fig. 4 ('an input molecule for Mol2Mol') and section 'Staged learning' ('This checkpoint can be reused as the agent later'); configs/staged_learning.toml header ('it is also possible to continue a run from any checkpoint file that is generated during the run').
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what_compose_still_has: Mol2Mol does not preserve the input molecule — 'the scaffold can change within the limits of the given similarity' — so the supplied molecule is a similarity anchor, not a state that is continued from. There is still no realized molecular history and no finite remaining-budget notion.

compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what: One trained model samples under any preference vector over its objective set with no retraining. A hypernetwork emits the prediction-head weights from the preference vector while the MPNN trunk is shared, and preferences are drawn from a Dirichlet during training so the model generalises across the simplex at inference. This is a genuine instance of 'goal information reshapes the model without retraining the molecular machinery', which is the shape of the COMPOSE frozen-process claim.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.evidence: arXiv:2302.04040v2 section 4.2: 'the hypernetwork h(.; phi) takes the preference vector lambda as inputs and outputs the weights theta_pred of prediction heads'; 'we propose only to condition the weights of prediction heads with hypernetworks, while sharing the weights of MPNN'; 'Our key motivation is to design a unified GFlowNet to sample candidates according to different reward functions, even ones not seen during training.' Code: model_pred_hyper.py::forward(self, ray); main.py generator(s, vec_data=weights, ...).
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what_compose_still_has: Only the scalarization WEIGHTS vary; the objective SET is fixed at training time and is architecturally baked in (n_objectives is the hypernetwork's input width and the surrogate's output width). A genuinely new objective requires a full retrain. Generation also starts from the empty molecule every time, so there is no source conditioning and no realized prefix.

compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what: Applies structural action masking at every action step, pre-softmax, recomputed after every action. This is a real pathwise constraint mechanism, not endpoint filtering, and the paper argues for it explicitly against the alternative of assigning minus infinity to violating endpoints.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.evidence: arXiv:2411.01667 section 2.1: 'To ensure chemical validity at every step of the molecule design process, we mask any action in the policy that would lead to a violation of valence constraints', implemented by 'we set the corresponding probability to zero in the distribution predicted by the policy (before re-normalizing the distribution)'; code molecule_design.py::update_action_mask, called at the end of take_action, and masked_log_probs_for_current_action_level setting logits[mask] = -inf.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what_compose_still_has: The maskable class in the released code is valence, atom type, atom count, no self-bonding, no re-bonding, and bond-order bounds. It does NOT include labeled subgraphs: the paper's ring-size and disallowed-bonding-pattern constraints are enforced instead by a TERMINAL minus-infinity filter in molecule_evaluator.py::infeasible_by_special_constraints on finished molecules, and there is no SMARTS or substructure matching anywhere in the repository. GraphXForm's action space is also strictly constructive, so a seed structure's atoms and bonds persist because nothing can be deleted rather than because a constraint holds. COMPOSE's C4d claim is a labeled motif preserved on a support that includes deletions and topology changes.

compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what: A new run can be launched from the exact realized molecule under a new objective using stock entry points: construct a new Estimator with the new objectives and call Sampler.sample(run_dir, mols_init=[switch_molecule] * num_mols). No patch is required, and the realized molecule is preserved as the starting state.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.evidence: https://github.com/bytedance/markov-molecular-sampling main.py (mols_init loading and the else-branch default 'CC') and sampler.py (Sampler.sample(run_dir, mols_init) signature). Verified absence of any mid-run switch hook in the same files.
compose_claims_a_baseline_does_natively.what_compose_still_has: It is a restart, not a continuation. The adapted proposal cannot be carried across a process boundary because no shipped code path saves it, so the editor is randomly re-initialised; the imitation dataset starts empty; and the temperature counter resets. MARS also has no remaining-budget concept at all — it is an infinite-horizon annealed sampler whose temperature is pinned at a 1e-2 floor from roughly step 450 onward. COMPOSE's claim is continuation with a finite remaining budget on a frozen process, not a fresh run.

global_fairness_rules: Property-oracle calls are the primary matched quantity. Wall time is reported, never matched, because the accelerator classes differ.

DECLARE THE COUNTING CONVENTION BEFORE ANY RUN, and use one convention for every method. The two live conventions differ materially and the choice is not neutral: (a) COMPOSE's own rule from configs/comparator_registry_v3.json counts every property-oracle evaluation including rejected candidates, particles, prescreened candidates and reranked endpoints; (b) PMO's Oracle.score_smi counts UNIQUE VALID CANONICAL SMILES only — duplicates hit a buffer and invalid SMILES return 0 without incrementing. Under (a) MARS's cost explodes and REINVENT's shrinks; under (b) the reverse. Published PMO numbers are only comparable under (b).

Objective-specific training oracle calls are counted. Report two totals for every method that trains per objective — with and without the training phase — because a reviewer may reasonably object to either convention.

A surrogate in the loop must be disclosed as a separate column. HN-GFN's 1000-call budget is spent against a learned proxy, not the true oracle; placing that beside a method that queries honestly is invalid in both directions.
Caching is allowed for every method, must use identical semantics (identical canonical SMILES implies identical score), and cache hits are reported separately.
Invalid or unscorable molecules are failed oracle proposals, not free actions.

Never claim equal support. MARS edits at fragment granularity, GraphGA recombines two parents, GraphXForm adds atoms and bonds without ever removing them, REINVENT decodes SMILES, HN-GFN attaches from a 105-block vocabulary, COMPOSE commits canonical successors of a frozen rewrite kernel.
A method with no notion of an intermediate molecule receives N/A on every pathwise metric, printed as N/A. Do not synthesise a trajectory from a GA lineage, a SMILES prefix, or a diffusion path.

Do not report literature numbers in a COMPOSE table without full protocol match. PMO's REINVENT is a 2.0-era reimplementation, not REINVENT 4, so PMO numbers and REINVENT 4 capabilities cannot be cited in the same row.

Use published defaults where they exist and record every deviation. PMO's own caution applies: REINVENT's performance is highly dependent on sigma and should be re-tuned whenever the environment changes, so using PMO's tuned sigma on a COMPOSE objective is itself a recorded deviation.
Non-commercial and unlicensed code is a provenance blocker, not a footnote. MARS is CC BY-NC 4.0 and DDSBM has no license at all.
